newsitem.title: INDIA: India keen to start talks with Kashmiri militants.
newsitem.headline: India keen to start talks with Kashmiri militants.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Sunday urged militants in the troubled Jammu and Kashmir state to lay down arms and start peace talks to end a seven-year-old rebellion in the state.
"...when guns are there, talks cannot take place," he told a news conference in state's summer capital Srinagar.

Dozens of guerrilla groups have been fighting since 1990 for Kashmir's independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan. India rules two-thirds of the region and Pakistan controls the rest. More than 20,000 people have died in the violence.
On Saturday Gujral offered unconditional talks to separatists but they have not responded so far.
"I have come here to further strengthen the bridges between the people of the State and the rest of India," Gujral said.
"During my two visits, the message the people of Jammu and Kashmir have given is that they have suffered a great deal from militancy and they want peace and development," he said.

Gujral said on Saturday he was keen to improve relations with Pakistan. "Through you I want to send a message across the border that we have extended our hand of friendship and cooperation which needs to be reciprocated."
India accuses Pakistan of arming Kashmiri militants, but Pakistan says it provides only moral and diplomatic support.
